1.finding: 3:1 bonus (08-Jul-2025) is reflected: EPS 4.47 / 5.34 / 7.24 FY23-25 are on the post-bonus count of 3.96 crore shares. A further 9,00,091 shares were placed at Rs 88 on 28-Oct-2025 (4.05 crore shares now).

2.finding: Operating cash flow Rs 1.34 / 11.49 / 32.09 cr FY23-25 against PAT Rs 15.67 / 21.14 / 28.67 cr: cumulative CFO/PAT 68.6% while revenue grew 34% a year. H1 FY26 CFO Rs 62.51 cr (PAT Rs 11.01 cr) as inventory and receivables were released; including H1, CFO exceeds PAT.

3.finding: Current tax 20.0% of cumulative FY23-25 PBT plus deferred tax (accelerated depreciation on new plants) 4.1%; income tax paid Rs 18.88 cr over three years.

4.finding: Promoters and relatives lend the company Rs 25.75 cr (Sep-2025) at interest (Rs 2.52 cr of interest in FY25) and rent it two properties; managerial pay is modest (Rs 0.66 cr to three promoter directors in FY25). Related-party transactions 3.14% of FY25 revenue. Disclosed and typical of a promoter-funded company.

5.finding: Amount-based fresh issue (Rs 191 cr): Rs 125 cr repays borrowings, Rs 18 cr buys out Siemens equipment leases, balance GCP (cap 25%). No fixed share count, so no objects floor.

8.finding: JSW Steel Coated Products supplied 90.61% of FY25 steel coils (authorised service partner since 2021); appliances 81.80% of FY25 product revenue; top customer (Amber Enterprises) 15.53% and top-10 67.44%. Typical of a service centre tied to one mill and the appliance PLI ecosystem.

9.finding: No contingent liabilities; capital commitments Rs 3.34 cr (Sep-2025).

R1.finding: Shah Shah & Shah (peer-reviewed); no qualifications. A previous auditor resigned in Aug-2021, before the current growth phase.

R2.finding: 25 delayed RoC filings over five years and a 2021 allotment to a promoter (for the Bombay Steels business transfer) filed with the wrong form and without MGT-14; compounding / adjudication application pending before the RoC. Procedural, rectified with additional fees; no penalty yet.

R3.finding: Fresh issue Rs 191 cr: monitoring agency mandatory; to be named in the RHP.

R6.finding: Smart Horizon Capital Advisors: past-issue track record is referenced to its website and not compiled in this run.

rationale.g1: Revenue Rs 590.88 cr -> Rs 755.26 cr -> Rs 1,055.71 cr (33.7% CAGR FY23-25) as Ghiloth (Rajasthan) and Sri City (AP) came up; H1 FY26 revenue Rs 491.51 cr, about 7% below the FY25 run-rate (pp. 44, 279). Capacity 220,506 MTPA with utilisation 46-66% in H1 FY26 (p. 123), so growth needs little new capacity. Neutral: flat FY26, then 8-10% with the appliance (AC, refrigerator) PLI build-out; Bear: FY26 down 5%; Bull: 6% then 10-15%.
rationale.m: Adjusted EBITDA (issuer KPI, net of other income) Rs 37.65 / 49.17 / 74.09 cr = 6.37% / 6.51% / 7.02% FY23-25 and 7.84% in H1 FY26 (p. 122); reproduces from the P&L. Neutral 7.0% (FY25); Bear 6.4% (FY23-24); Bull 7.8% (H1 FY26).
rationale.nwc: Trade working capital 17.2% / 17.8% / 17.0% of revenue FY23-25 (p. 278); issuer's NWC days 61-73 (p. 123). Neutral 17%.
rationale.capex: No IPO capex (the Rs 18 cr lease buy-out replaces lease liabilities, which are included in net debt). Base capex Rs 34.61 cr in FY25 (p. 280) was an expansion year; k is implied from it and is conservative given 46-66% utilisation. Net debt Rs 259.53 cr = Sep-2025 borrowings Rs 270.94 cr + lease liabilities Rs 15.99 cr - cash and bank Rs 19.48 cr - Oct-2025 placement proceeds Rs 7.92 cr. Net worth Rs 101.99 cr = Sep-2025 Rs 94.07 cr + placement Rs 7.92 cr.
